 Russia and Ukraine Launch Massive Missile and Drone Attacks Ahead of End-of-War Negotiations
 Jung Seong-jin 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.07 22:26 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ A kindergarten damaged by a Russian missile attack in Kyiv, Ukraine, on the 7th (local time). 
 As Ukraine and Russia prepare for trilateral negotiations with the United States next week, both sides continue to exchange massive attacks targeting each other. 
 In Ukraine, Russian missile and drone attacks left at least nine people injured and caused power outages across five regions, while Russia also reported one civilian death and attacks on an oil refinery and other facilities. 
 Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated via X on the 7th (local time) that Russia launched 36 ballistic missiles targeting the capital Kyiv and its surrounding areas overnight, mobilizing 172 drones for the attack. 
 President Zelenskyy noted that Russia's latest attack primarily targeted energy infrastructure, destroying substations across multiple regions, and that a kindergarten was also hit, injuring a child among a total of nine injured individuals. 
 Zelenskyy urged the United States to expand its support and strengthen sanctions against Russia, stating, "When Russia tries to plunge the city of Kyiv, home to millions, and all of Ukraine into darkness, Ukraine must not be left to fight this alone." 
 The Ukrainian Ministry of Energy announced in a statement that day that Russian attacks on energy infrastructure have cut off electricity supplies in five regions, including Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Kyiv, Zhytomyr, and Kharkiv oblasts, AFP reported. 
 The Kyiv city government announced that a northern bridge crossing the Dnipro River was attacked and closed to traffic. 
 Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko told AP, "The energy supply situation in the capital is very difficult, and it is also affecting the city's heating and water supply systems." 
 The Russian Ministry of Defense confirmed the attack in a statement that day, claiming that the northern bridge in Kyiv was being used to transport weapons, military equipment, and special equipment for the Ukrainian military. 
 The Russian defense ministry added that it targeted an industrial facility in Kyiv producing Flamingo missiles, power plants, and substations, as well as a plant producing ammunition, explosives, and gunpowder in the Kyiv region. 
 The Ukrainian emergency services announced that the death toll from a Russian attack using multiple 3-ton bombs on a humanitarian aid distribution center in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, southern Ukraine, on the 3rd has risen to 55. 
 Dozens of people remain missing, and emergency services are continuing search operations. 
 Meanwhile, in Russia, local authorities stated on the 7th that one resident was killed when a private home in Belgorod Oblast was hit by a Ukrainian drone attack. 
 The Russian Ministry of Defense announced that it shot down 411 Ukrainian drones overnight across 10 regions, including Belgorod Oblast. 
 Local administrative authorities also reported that the Saratov oil refinery and commercial warehouses and production facilities in Oryol were damaged. 
 (Photo: AP, Yonhap News)
